newsitem.title: UK: UK's ITC consults on Utd News TV licences.
newsitem.headline: UK's ITC consults on Utd News TV licences.

text.p: Britain's Independent Television Commission (ITC) said on Thursday it was checking whether the control by United News & Media of regional TV licences was against the public interest, given its newspaper businesses.

United News operates the ITV licences for southern England through its Meridian unit and eastern England with its control of Anglia Television. It also publishes three national newspapers -- The Express, Express on Sunday and Daily Star plus a number of local newspapers in the Anglia TV area.
The company effectively doubled in size this year when United News merged with TV and financial services group MAI.
The Broadcasting Act passed in July eased restrictions on cross media ownership but introduced the public interest test.

Television watchdog the ITC must take into account the desirability of promoting plurality of ownership in the broadcasting and newspaper industries and the economic and market impact of the arrangement.
The ITC invited comments on the issue by December 13. It is up to the ITC to propose a solution if it finds an ownership structure does create problems.
In its first such decision, the ITC ruled last month that the acquisition of regional newspaper group Caledonian Publishing by Scottish Television would not operate against the public interest.
